# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1–38 (Updated 2026-10-13, Final Revision 9)

## Setting and Time
- **Current Period**: Spring of tenth year after Waterloo (1831). Story spans from Sunday, 26th April dinner (Chapters 1–35) through Chapter 36 (winter into summer) to Chapters 37–38 (spring/early summer). Emperor of China dinner scheduled Monday, 8th July; election for Westminster borough Tuesday, 9th July. Chapters 37–38 set in Harrowgate hill farms, coastal towns, Dunholt village, Staveton harbor town, transitions to London.
- **Key Locations**: London (Welbeck Street, Grosvenor Square, Abchurch Lane, Beargarden Club, Bruton Street, Queen's Gate, Islington, City Road Music-Hall, Cannon Street Hotel, Euston Square); Coventry Island; Queen's Crawley; Southend; Harrowgate; Lowestoft; Dunholt; Staveton; Gulton; coastal towns; rural areas (Sheep's Acre Farm, etc.).

## Major Deaths
John Sedley, Mr. Osborne, Joseph Sedley, Colonel Rawdon Crawley, Sir Pitt, Wevie Lindner (died winter, buried Salmere). Conar Hollett (drowned crossing estuary at Gulton; no body seen; Halan Hollett reported it at inn).

## Rebecca's Arc
Never became Lady Crawley; styles herself so. Son (Sir Rawdon) receives allowance but refuses to see her. Appears wealthy at Bath/Cheltenham, busies herself with piety and Charity Lists.

## Amelia and William Dobbin
Married at Ostend; Amelia initiated encounter. Dobbin quit service, rented "the Evergreens" (Hampshire). Devoted father; daughter Jane his pride.

## Lady Carbury and Family

**Lady Carbury**: Welbeck Street resident. Authored "Criminal Queens." Crushed by "Evening Pulpit" review; praised by "Morning Breakfast Table" (Mr. Broune). Rejected Mr. Broune's proposal via letter; full of regrets; in debt. Now **overdrawing her account at bank** (Chapter 38).

**Felix Carbury**: Director of South Central Pacific and Mexican Railway. Won £2,000 from Lord Grasslough, £400 from Miles Grendall at gaming. **Chapter 38 (COMPLETED)**: Elopement finalized. Didon delivered full £250 to Felix at Beargarden Club Monday 4 P.M., envelope "soft and fat with rich enclosures." Felix counted notes in waiting-room; all present. Upon receipt, Didon departed after asking "C'est tout en règle?" Felix understood he must now certainly go to New York. Felix reflected bitterly: Melmotte held more of his money than he held of Melmotte's. Dined at club Monday evening, planned to visit mother after, take passage Tuesday at City in name "Walter Jones" (felt intrigue becoming very deep), spend Tuesday evening with Ruby at Music Hall, depart Wednesday 5 P.M. for Liverpool. Tuesday evening at Music Hall: remained 10 P.M. to nearly midnight, very angry at Ruby's non-appearance; decided he would claim to her that he devoted last night in England to telling her of departure—she broke appointment; her fault, not his. After receiving passage money, went back to club despite understanding danger; found Dolly Longestaffe and Miles Grendall smoking pipes in smoking-room. Refused three-handed loo; whispered petition to Grendall that I.O.U.s be converted to cash. Had been drinking freely before going to Welbeck Street; took glass of brandy upon re-entering club. Standing with back to fireplace (others present), held up scraps of paper, asked loudly if any fellow would buy them for five shillings in pound. Called Grendall up to card-room with Dolly as witness; Grendall refused, said no one playing that night, would be there tomorrow. **Wednesday morning, 5 A.M.: Departed Welbeck Street per schedule for Liverpool, presumably boarded S.S. "Adriatic."** (Plan: boards without acknowledging Marie/Didon until at sea.)

**Henrietta Carbury**: Rejected Roger's suit (too young, age disparity). Paul returned "as still dear friend" within week, promising not to see her three months. Wore rose from Roger's room. Roger declared love anew (Chapter 32 evening); determination unshaken. Paul thoroughly in love with her. Chapter 36: Paul visited her at Welbeck Street; she told mother loves someone else and praises Roger as "rock of strength."

## Ruby Ruggles and Suitors

**Ruby Ruggles**: Pretty servant/maid to Mrs. Pipkin at Islington. **Chapter 38**: Danced with Felix at City Road Music-Hall. When Felix refused marriage, Roger Carbury warned her forcefully against him; extracted promise not to see him again. Wrote Felix letter of regret; he replied tersely: Tuesday (final night before New York departure). Sought to attend Tuesday dance; Mrs. Pipkin refused. After pleading, Mrs. Pipkin reluctantly agreed Ruby could go "just this once." **Ruby attended Tuesday evening at Music Hall; Felix was there 10 P.M. to nearly midnight but (text indicates) Ruby did not appear or they did not connect—Felix noted "non-appearance of Ruby Ruggles" and was "very angry."** Felix rationalized he had devoted last night to telling her of departure; her fault she missed it.

**John Crumb**: Country lover from Suffolk, "Bungay mealman." Chapter 35: Attempted to take Ruby's hand; Ruby fled. Rode to Carbury Hall searching for her. Chapter 37: Visited Roger at Carbury Manor, expressed anguish about Felix, declared willingness to "swing for it" if seduced. Roger assured him Ruby good and promised Mrs. Pipkin supervision. Resolved to send Mrs. Pipkin price of new blue cloak via Mixet's letter and money order.

**Daniel Ruggles**: Holds Sheep's Acre Farm. Violent; pulled Ruby by hair. Told Roger suitor should speak his mind.

**Mrs. Pipkin**: Ruby's aunt at Islington; lets lodgings. Chapter 38: Feared Ruby would escape; reluctantly allowed her to attend Tuesday evening at Music Hall after pleas.

## Paul Montague and Mrs. Winifrid Hurtle

**Paul's Crisis (Chapter 37)**: At Lowestoft, told Mrs. Hurtle he cannot join his lot with her—his heart elsewhere; her antecedents caused friends to warn him. Mrs. Hurtle responded with fury. Confessed she shot a man in Oregon; saved herself. Divorced Caradoc Hurtle (drunkard, scoundrel) under Kansas law on grounds of cruelty and drunkenness (he made no appearance; court granted divorce). Questioned why condemned for protecting herself. Paul thought words may have been necessary in Oregon. She called him coward, said he trembles between her and Roger. Declared she would not stay, return Monday, resolve what to do, seek means of punishing him. Expected him Monday. Said if afraid to come, she would come to him and tell her story. Paul said he would wait upon her on return to town but would not fix day; promised to write.

**Mrs. Hurtle's Aftermath (Chapter 37–38)**: After Paul departed, fell on knees, gave way to flood of tears. Questioned: Should she never know rest? With heart of hearts loved this young Englishman. She had run over on what seemed vain chance after receiving his letter. Knew Englishwomen would avoid her when past known; scorned and feared in eastern cities; name proverb for violence in far West. Hesitation in accepting marriage arose from her own conviction of unfitness. Circumstances made her what she was; could not alter them now. Gradually believed in his love, lost herself in it, told herself she would change. Almost known it could not be so. **Chapter 38**: Returned from Lowestoft Monday; made trivial excuse to Mrs. Pipkin (place windy, too cold, disliked hotel). Mrs. Pipkin glad to see her back. Has not sent letter to Paul in pocket-book; still keeps it, at moments thinking to send it, at others told herself never surrender last hope till every stone turned. Might still be possible to shame him into marriage. Promised Mrs. Pipkin she would speak to Ruby (though aware of her unfitness for task—knew nothing of country; not single friend but Paul; had run after him with little discretion as Ruby after her lover). **Paul returned to London by mail train evening, sure he would avoid meeting Mrs. Hurtle in railway-carriage.**

## The Melmottes

**Augustus Melmotte**: Chairman, South Central Pacific and Mexican Railway. Chapter 37–38: Extremely busy with electioneering speeches, Committee members, dinner orders, commercial affairs. Told Felix only entitled to shares for £600 now, will see it put right. Proposed Paul Mexican embassy; tone dubious to Paul. Expressed relief dinner would be over. Received Board meeting call; ran off to meeting at Cannon Street Hotel.

**Marie Melmotte**: **Chapter 38 (COMPLETED)**: Elopement executed successfully. Sat up all night packing/unpacking treasures with Didon; asked about American clergyman marrying them on board; discussed wedding dress fit for occasion. Didon thought man if sufficiently paid would marry them; scolded Marie for nonsense but worked hard. Determined to go without food morning so no suspicion raised by cups/plates; would get refreshment at railway-station. **At 6 A.M. Wednesday, Robert departed first with big boxes (ten pounds already in pocket). Marie and Didon followed in second cab with smaller luggage. No interference; very civil man at Euston Square gave them tickets, attempted French. Determined not to speak English till ship out at sea. Got very bad tea and uneatable food at station; Marie's restrained excitement so great food unnecessary. Took seats without impediment; departed.** As drew near Liverpool, Didon explained must still be careful; not declare at once destination so everyone at station knew they going on board packet for New York. Had time; must leisurely look for big boxes; need say nothing about steam packet till in cab. Marie's big box directed "Madame Racine, Passenger to Liverpool"; Didon's similarly. Didon declared anxiety would not be over till ship moving under her. Marie sure all dangers over—if only Sir Felix safe on board. **Felix was actually at same time in Welbeck Street, striving to find oblivion for distressing situation and loss of money, alleviation for racking temples, beneath bedclothes.**

## The Longestaffes

**Sir Merton Longestaffe**: Determined no London expenses. Desires to sell Pickering and disembarrass Caversham. Dolly refused consent unless half produce given to him.

**Adolphus (Dolly) Longestaffe**: Has rooms in Bruton Street. **Chapter 38**: Arrangement made: £5,000 pay off all tradesmen's debts, leave him comfortably possessed; other £20,000 make his property free. Returned demanding cheque on Melmotte's bank payable to his own. Has not yet received single ten-pound note from sale. Threatens to employ Mr. Squercum if money not paid quickly. Present at club smoking-room Monday evening with Miles Grendall.

**Georgiana Longestaffe**: Made protest against Melmottes. Following morning received invitation to stay with them. By Sunday, present at Grosvenor Square.

## South Central Pacific and Mexican Railway Scheme

**The Enterprise**: Railway from Salt Lake City through New Mexico/Arizona into Mexico, terminating Vera Cruz. Approximately 2,000 miles. Stock at par; shares sold at premium. Directors understood fortune made by floating shares, not building railway.

**London Directorate**: Melmotte (chairman), Lord Alfred Grendall, Sir Felix Carbury (now departed for America), Samuel Cohenlupe (MP for Staines), Lord Nidderdale, Paul Montague.

## Roger Carbury
Nearly forty. Never owed shilling he couldn't pay. Firmly opposed Melmotte connection on principle. Soft heart; knows Lady Carbury false and Felix worthless. Declared love to Henrietta anew; determination unshaken. Visited Ruby at Islington; warned her against Felix; extracted promise not to see him again; spoke to Mrs. Pipkin about late hours. Encountered Paul and Mrs. Hurtle at Lowestoft; greeted coldly; reproved Paul severely regarding conduct with Mrs. Hurtle. Counselled marriage with her would be destruction. Upon Paul's return, expressed satisfaction: "Let her follow you, and bear it. Of course you must suffer the effects of your own imprudence."

## Minor Characters
**Lord Alfred Grendall**: Nearly overwhelmed by electioneering; nearly in rebellion. Burdened with seating arrangements.

**Miles Grendall**: Secretary to Melmotte. Does not pay debts of honour. Present at club smoking-room Monday evening with Dolly.

**Didon**: Marie's attendant; **executed elopement plan: presented Melmotte's cheque to bank, obtained £250, delivered to Felix at Beargarden Monday 4 P.M. Held tickets under name "Madame Racine." Departed 6 A.M. Wednesday with Marie in cab; faithful to her throughout; declared anxiety would not be over till ship moving under them. To receive £50 before boarding.**

**Father John Barham**: Priest, Beccles.

**Sally Hockett**: Witnessed Daniel Ruggles pulling Ruby by hair.

**Mr. Squercum**: Lawyer threatened employment by Dolly.

**Robert** (servant): **Marie's man; departed 6 A.M. Wednesday with big boxes, ten pounds already in pocket.**

**Provincial Figures (Chapters 37–38)**: Halan Hollett, Thivie Brackwood, Votho Brackwood, Jozek Hollett, Garald Stenworth, Nylis Corrett, Rolde (child born to Nylis Corrett and Orbin Stenworth, named Rolde Stenworth; family lived in Staveton), Orbin Stenworth, Ilrine Corrett, and others in rural villages and harbor towns.
